title: Shield vs. Bow + More
text: “…Sigh.”

My Father looks utterly exasperated. A duel with the Shield Hero… that’s just beyond foolish. Well, I was the one doing that in the first world, though. Thinking about it now, I just want to punch myself.
“For a Hero to be using slaves… I’d only heard rumors about it, but if Lord Itsuki objects, then I shall order it. Duel!”
Perhaps because he knew what had happened beforehand, his sigh was a deep one.
“If Lord Itsuki wins, all of the Shield Hero’s slaves will be freed; if the Shield Hero wins, the matter will be dropped.”
“…I don’t think that’s a fair deal, though?”
“In what way? Justice will be proven!”
“Justice, huh… I have no reason to fight, and does Itsuki understand that I have very few means of attack?”
“There’s more than enough incentive. It’s the right to command slaves as you please.”
“Think carefully about the point of being granted a right you already have as if it were a reward.”
That’s totally pointless. It’s infuriating to have some piece of Trash condescendingly grant you permission for something you already possess. My blood’s boiling, too.
“Well then, shall I take care of Itsuki in your Father’s place? I’m practically your Father’s slave, after all.”

That’s right—I’m both The Love Hunter and a Slave of Love. If it’s a command from Filo-tan, I’ll make anything happen. And if it’s a command from Filo-tan’s Father, it’s the same as a command from Filo-tan herself.
“I’ve never once thought of Motoyasu-kun as a slave…”
“Thank you! But I am The Love Hunter who lives for you, Father. So please just think of me as a Slave of Love as well.”
“No, I don’t understand a word of what you’re saying.”
“Either way, since I’m under your command, Father, wouldn’t it be fine for me to fight Itsuki on your behalf?”
Itsuki is nothing but a pushover when it comes to me. It’s actually harder to hold back just enough so he doesn’t die. If I pin Itsuki to the ground with my attacks, he’ll surely admit defeat.
“Why is the Spear Hero meddling in the Shield Hero’s duel? There’s no way I’d grant permission for that!”
“That’s right! This is a duel between me and Naofumi! Don’t just barge in on us!”
This is really starting to get on my nerves. In that case, I’m sorry to my Father, but should I just kill Itsuki? Would that cause the loop to restart?

Well then, maybe I’ll just chop off his arms and legs—just enough so he doesn’t die? If I keep it to a level where he can be healed with recovery magic, will that teach him a lesson he’ll never forget? The castle soldiers are trying to subdue Keel, Sakura-chan, Yuki-chan, and Kou.
“Let them go! Don’t mess with me! Big bro!”
Keel hurls the soldier who lunged at him across the room and races over to his Father.
“You’re trying to bully my brother! I’ll never forgive you!”
“No, Keel… ‘Bullying’…”
Keel growls, “Grrrr,” radiating a murderous aura from every pore. Sakura draws her sword as well, and Yuki and the others assume battle stances.

“Do you dare defy me, the King? So you’re all just underlings of the Shield, are you? No—some slave marks prevent their bearers from speaking anything that displeases their master. Summon a mage immediately to remove them!”
Mind control is actually your specialty, isn’t it! Father claps his hands loudly to draw everyone’s attention.
“…Fine. I’ll just have a one-on-one duel with Itsuki, right?”

“Who said anything about a one-on-one duel? This is a battle between the Shield Hero and Lord Itsuki’s party! My word is law! If you don’t comply, I’ll confiscate the Shield Hero’s slaves by force if I have to.”

……Father looked completely exasperated. One against many… Just how many foolish things does he have to say before he’s satisfied? I know this breaks the promise I made to my Father last time, but I simply cannot stand by and watch such an outrageous act.
All right, let’s kill Trash and Crimson Swine right now. Just as I was about to put my strength into my spear, Itsuki interrupted Trash and said,
“That’s far too underhanded! It’s obviously supposed to be a one-on-one duel!”
“What are you doing?!”
Rin has finally joined the fray. In the first world, this didn’t happen until after the duel was over… Could this be the result of sowing distrust toward the kingdom?
Well then, let me explain the situation for now. I’ll tell the version that puts us in a better light… Just telling the truth seems like it’ll give us the upper hand.
“When Itsuki took issue with his father enslaving people and complained, the king is now trying to force them into a duel.”
“Slaves? Is Naofumi enslaving people? Are all his companions slaves, by any chance?”
Why is he bringing this up now? Ren turns his gaze toward Keel.
“I didn’t really pay much attention, but since you guys seemed to get along well, I assumed you were companions.”
“I may be my big bro’s slave, but I respect him as a hero! He’s totally different from Trash like you guys!”
Ren began staring at Kuzu and Itsuki with a cold gaze. If this keeps up, the commotion is only going to get worse.
“So when my father agreed to a one-on-one duel after Itsuki’s whims were met, the king declared that it wouldn’t be a one-on-one duel, but a battle between my father and Itsuki’s entire group.”
“Huh!? That’s way too unfair!”
“Exactly! Someone like Naofumi—I can handle him all by myself.”

They really did give Itsuki too much preferential treatment. They said something similar when it was my turn, but I thought it was unfair, so I insisted on a one-on-one duel. Realizing how bad the situation had gotten, Trash wiped his sweat and tried to cover it up.
“I misspoke. Therefore, I hereby declare a duel between Lord Itsuki, the Bow Hero, and the Shield Hero.”
Well, even so, Ren’s distrust hasn’t been completely dispelled. Realizing they can’t subdue Keel or Sakura-chan, the kingdom’s people will quietly back down.
“Big bro! Are you okay?”
“I am.”

I approach my Father and ask him. This situation is already close to the original history, but it’s a completely different scenario. Both Itsuki and Ren, who were once far from the truth, are now in a situation closer to the truth than they were in the future. …Although Itsuki is sticking to the justice he believes in, and Ren’s suspicions toward the kingdom are growing.

“Ideally, it would be fine if Keel and Sakura-chan were here… but it seems the people from the kingdom want to enjoy watching me lose. If I don’t go along with this now, who knows what they might do. I’ll play along with them a little.”
“What do you plan to do, then?”
No matter how strong he is, the fact remains that my Father has very few offensive options. This is an undeniable truth. Depending on the situation, I’ll step in to protect him.

“It’s okay—it’s not like I don’t have a secret plan. Just because my offensive options are limited doesn’t mean I have no way to win. I want to let Itsuki… experience that firsthand. He’s in on the plot to set a trap for me, and I’m getting pretty fed up with his attitude by now.”
“But…”
My father smiled as he stroked the heads of Keel and Sakura, who were meowing worriedly.
“Don’t worry, it’ll be fine… I’ll definitely come out victorious.”

Stepping out into the castle courtyard, my father and Itsuki lock eyes in the center of the circle of spectators. What kind of shield is the Father wielding? From the looks of it, it’s a spiked shield… Did he acquire that in Siltvelt?
Well, something like that probably won’t raise any suspicion. What’s he planning to do? The only plausible option is to use a counterattack effect to completely deplete Itsuki’s HP.

The Father hasn’t mastered Magic yet. As for using potions for healing… that probably won’t be allowed. It’s practically a public execution… I feel like the barbaric acts I committed in the past are about to be reenacted right before my eyes. It feels like my heart is about to burst.

“Now, let the duel between the Bow Hero and the Shield Hero begin! Victory or defeat will be determined by whether one is cornered to the point of receiving the finishing blow, or by conceding defeat.”

Testing to see if his wrist moves smoothly and cracking his knuckles, Father takes his stance. Ah… I’m overcome with the urge to step in front of him right now and protect him, but he insists he’ll be fine. Suppressing that impulse, all we can do is watch in silence.
“Fighting Naofumi, a weak class, will only lead to a quick result, but it’s for the sake of justice. You’d best admit defeat early.”
“I’ll teach you a lesson, Itsuki. In most online games, so-called ‘tank’ classes are actually pretty strong in PvP. I’ll drive home just how terrifying a shield that can’t attack really is.”

My father probably has far more experience with online games than either me or Ren. After all, he was reportedly involved in running a major guild that ranked third on the server. And that’s not all—he’s got a real knack for it, too.
“Well then—”

Of course, the rules are probably different in this world. But Father has the flexibility to adapt. In fact, among all of us who thought shield classes were a losing proposition, he was the strongest. So, even though I have a slight sense of unease, I believe Father will win.
“Let’s settle this!”
